translations.text: And after seven days, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
And I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be mute and will not be a man who rebukes them, for they are a rebellious house.
And you shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, strengthen your arms, and prophesy against it.

And I said, “Far be it, Lord God of Israel, that I should ever have defiled myself with unclean things! From my birth until now, I have never eaten anything that died on its own or was torn by wild beasts, nor has any unclean meat entered my mouth.”
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
And I will lay the corpses of the Israelites strewn before your images, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.
They shall put on sackcloth, and terrors shall cover them. Shame shall be on every face, and baldness on every head.
I went in and saw, and there was every likeness of creeping things and animals, worthless abominations; and I saw all the idols of the house of Israel painted all around them.

And seventy men from among the elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them, stood before them. Each had a censer in his hand, and the smoke of the incense rose and gathered like a cloud.

And the Lord said to me, “Son of man, do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing there in the darkness, each secretly in his own chamber? For they say, ‘The Lord has abandoned us and does not look upon the earth.’”
And the cherubim stood on the right side of the temple when the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court.
And their whole bodies, their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around their four wheels.
Multiply your corpses in that city, and fill its roads with the wounded.

And you, son of man, prepare yourself equipment for exile, and go into exile by day before them. You shall go into exile from your own place to another place before them, so that they may see, for they are a rebellious house.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, what is this proverb you have in the land of Israel, which says, “The days are far off, and every vision has perished”?
Have you not seen false visions and recounted worthless divinations, saying, “Thus says the Lord,” when I, the Lord, have not spoken?

And I will stretch out my hand against the prophets who saw falsehoods and spoke worthless things. They shall not stand in the council of my people, nor shall they be recorded in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel. And they shall know that I am the Lord GOD.
And men from among the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.
Son of man, these men have set their thoughts in their hearts and placed the torments of their wrongdoing before their faces. Am I really to give them an answer?
Son of man, if a land sins against me by committing a transgression, I will stretch out my hand against it, break its supply of bread, send famine upon it, and remove people and animals from it.
And I will make the land a desolation because they fell into transgressions, says the Lord GOD.

Multiply, for I made you like a plant of the field. And you multiplied and grew, and you came and entered the cities of cities. Your breasts drooped and your hair grew, but you were naked and exposed.
And I clothed you in embroidered garments and put blue shoes on you. I wrapped fine linen around your waist and covered you with silk.
I put earrings and pendants in your ears and a crown of glory on your head.
And the fame of your beauty spread among all the nations, for your beauty was perfect through the splendor I had placed upon you, says the Lord Adonai.
And you took your glorious ornaments, made from my gold and silver that I had given you, and made yourself male images and prostituted yourself with them.

And this was more appalling than all your prostitution and abominations. You did not remember the days of your childhood, when you were naked, exposed, and wallowing in your blood, from which you were brought to life.

But this was the lawlessness of your sister Sodom: arrogance amid an abundance of bread and a lavish supply of wine. She and her daughters lived indulgently; she and her daughters abounded in these things, but they did not extend a hand to the poor and needy.
So that you may receive your punishment and be disgraced for everything you did to provoke me to anger.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the Lord.
And you shall say: Thus says the Lord Adonai: A great eagle, with great wings, a wide wingspan, and abundant talons, resolved to enter Lebanon and took the choicest of the cedars.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

And he will rebel against him by sending messengers to Egypt to give him horses and many troops. Will he prosper? Will he survive? Will one who does such contrary things and breaks the covenant survive?
And Pharaoh will not wage war alongside him with great strength or a large army. He will build siege ramps and platforms for shooting to destroy many lives.
For he despised the oath and broke the covenant. Look, I delivered him into his hands and did all this to him. Will he survive?
And in all his escapes, in all his battles, they will fall by the sword. I will scatter his survivors to every wind, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken.
Let none of the offenses he committed or the injustices he perpetrated be remembered. Rather, he will live through the righteousness he practiced.
And he went about among lions and became a lion. He learned to seize prey and became a devourer of people.
And fire came out from its choicest branches and consumed it, and there was no strong rod in it. A people serves as a parable of mourning, and it will become a lament.
Son of man, speak to these elders of the house of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord Adonai: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, I will give you no answer, says the Lord Adonai.
And I gave them my commands and showed them my ordinances, which a person shall carry out and live by them.

And the house of Israel provoked me in the wilderness. They did not walk according to my commands and rejected my ordinances, which, if a person carries them out, he will live by them. They greatly profaned my Sabbaths, and I said I would pour out my wrath in the wilderness to destroy them.
Just as I passed judgment on your fathers there in the wilderness, when I brought them out of the land of the Egyptians, so I will judge you, says the Lord, the Lord God.
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and set your face against Jerusalem. Look toward their sanctuaries and prophesy against the land of Israel.

So that their hearts may break and the weakened may multiply at all their gates, for they have been handed over to slaughter by the sword. It has been made beautiful by its gleam and made fit for slaughter.
And you, prepare and arrange a road for the sword to enter through Rabbah of the Ammonites, against Judea and against Jerusalem within it.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Those who were near you and those far from you will mock you and say, “Your name has been disgraced, because you have multiplied your lawless deeds.”
Son of man, look: the house of Israel has become a mixed alloy to me, like copper, iron, tin, lead, and silver mixed together in a furnace.
The sons of Babylon came to her bed to lie with her, and they defiled her through their prostitution. She was defiled with them, and her soul became disgusted with them.
For thus says the Lord God: “Bring an army against them, and cast turmoil and plunder upon them.”
The people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things you are doing mean?”
The word of the Lord came to me and said:

“I will bring you down to those who descend into the pit, to the people of ancient times. I will make you dwell in the depths of the earth, like the ancient ruins, with those who descended long ago into the pit, so that you will no longer be inhabited or stand in the land of the living.”
You shall say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrances to the sea and trades with peoples from many islands: “Thus says the Lord God to Tyre:
Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt was made into your sailcloth, to clothe you in splendor. Purple and blue cloth from the islands of [?] became the adornment of your coverings.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
“You were blameless throughout your days, from the day you were established until injustices were found in you.”
Therefore thus says the Lord God: “Look, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy both people and animals from among you.”
Thus says Adonai the Lord: “The supports of Egypt will collapse, and the pride of its strength will fall. From Migdol to Syene they will fall within it by the sword,” says Adonai the Lord.
Water nourished it; the deep waters made it grow tall. It brought its rivers around its plantations and spread its dense growth among all the trees of the field.
When it fell, it became a resting place for all the birds of heaven, and all the wild animals came to its branches.
There are Edom, its kings, and all its rulers, who surrendered their strength to the blows of the sword. They too lay with the wounded, with those who descended into the pit.

There are all the rulers of the north and all those commanders of Assyria who descended wounded. Despite the terror inspired by their strength, they lay in shame, uncircumcised, with those wounded by swords, and bore their torments with those who descended into the pit.
If he sees a sword coming against the land, he shall blow the trumpet and warn the people.

When I say to the righteous person, “You will surely live,” and he trusts in his righteousness and commits lawlessness, none of his righteous deeds shall be remembered. Instead, he shall die because of the lawlessness he committed.
“Is this what you say: ‘The way of the Lord is not right’? I will judge each of you according to your ways, house of Israel.”

And you, son of man: the children of your people go about murmuring about you beside the walls and at the doors of their houses. They say to one another, each man to his brother, “Let us gather and go and hear the messages that have come from the Lord.”

Now they come to you as people gathering for an assembly, and my people sit before you to hear your words, but they do not carry them out, for falsehood is in their mouths, and their hearts follow their own impurity.

“I will bring them out from the nations and gather them from the countries. I will bring them into their own land and pasture them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys, and in every inhabited place in the land.”
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Therefore prophesy and say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Look, I will open your graves and bring you out of your graves, my people, and bring you into the land of Israel.
And you will know that I am the Lord when I open your graves and bring you out of your graves, my people.
And I will establish a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will give to them and multiply them, and I will place my sanctuary among them forever.

To seize spoil and plunder their possessions, to lay my hand upon the land that was devastated and is inhabited, and upon the people gathered from many nations, who have acquired possessions and estates and live in the heart of the land.
And you will eat fat until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk, from the sacrifices that I slaughter for you.
And they will bear their disgrace and the wrongdoing they committed, when I settle them peacefully in their own land, with no one to terrify them.
And they will know that I am the Lord their God when I appear to them among the nations. I will gather them into their own land and no longer leave any of them anywhere else.
And the gate's guardrooms faced one another, three on this side and three on that side. All three had the same dimensions, and the archways on this side and that side had the same dimensions.
And its guardrooms, archways, and recesses had the same dimensions, and its windows and archways were all around: fifty cubits in length and twenty-five in width.

And the width of the sides of the upper gate, according to the [?] of the sides of the walls, toward the upper part around the house, so that the house would be spacious above and below; from these they go up to the upper stories, and from the middle stories to the third story.
And the partition opposite the [?], on the seaward side of the passage, was seventy cubits in length. The width of the partition's wall was five cubits, and its length was ninety cubits.
From the floors to the ceilings, cherubim and palm trees were carved.
And he brought me to the gate that faced east and led me out through it.
And the base was four cubits, and above the base the horns were one cubit.
The portion dedicated from the land will belong to the priests who serve in the sanctuary, those who approach to serve the Lord. They will have a place set apart for the house of their sanctuary.

And the priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering and sprinkle it on the thresholds of the house, on the four corners of the temple, on the altar, and on the thresholds of the gate of the inner court.
And on that day the ruler will offer one bull from the herd as a sin offering for himself, for the house, and for all the people of the land.

And when the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals, whoever enters by way of the north gate to bow down will leave by way of the south gate, and whoever enters by way of the south gate will leave by way of the north gate. He must not return by way of the gate through which he entered, but must go straight out that way.
And the ruler will be among them: when they enter, he will enter with them, and when they leave, he will leave with them.
And with it, morning by morning, a grain offering of one-sixth of a measure and one-third of a sextarius of oil mixed into the fine flour—a grain offering to the Lord, an everlasting ordinance.
And on the south, southward, from Teman and from the palm grove as far as the waters of Meribah-kadesh, extending to the Great Sea: this is the southern and southward boundary.
And the workers of the city, from all the tribes of Israel, will cultivate it.
And on the eastern side, four thousand five hundred by measure, with three gates: one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, and one gate of Dan.
